findings.title: Every iOS continuous-capture manifest is refused at seal: the Swift result's device object lacks screenW/screenH/densityDpi/orientation that the server validator requires
findings.userImpact: No iOS screen recording can ever be sealed. The user records, uploads every segment, stages, opens Capture, taps Finish & Sign, and continuous-complete answers CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID. The reserved record is eventually reaped; the recording is lost as evidence.
findings.legalImpact: UC-5 is documented as code-complete / PASS (docs/uc6-release-acceptance.md:141) while it cannot produce a single sealed record.
findings.reproduction: ProovraBroadcastResult.toJsMap (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:58-63) emits device = {platform:'ios', osVersion, model, appVersion} only. stopContinuousCapture resolves that map (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.swift:102-104) → buildContinuousManifest copies result.device verbatim (continuous-capture.ts:121) → manifestJson carried to /continuous-complete → validateScreenContinuousManifest loops over screenW/screenH/densityDpi (screen-continuous-manifest.ts:286-288) and returns 'invalid device.screenW' → continuous-capture.service.ts:99-101 throws CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID.
findings.observed: Swift device map has 4 keys; validator requires 8. The UC-5 integration test hand-builds a device with screenW:1179, screenH:2556, densityDpi:460, orientation:'portrait' (uc5-ios-screen-capture.integration.test.ts:253-262) that the Swift never produces, so the suite passes against a fictional payload; the native contract test compares method/event NAMES only (native-module-contract.test.mjs:75-99).
findings.expected: The iOS result carries every device field the server requires (UIScreen.main.nativeBounds/scale for pixels, a documented densityDpi convention for iOS, orientation), or the validator accepts an iOS-specific device shape; and a test drives the manifest from the exact map the Swift emits.
findings.rootCause: The iOS device shape was never reconciled with the manifest schema; server tests fabricate the device object instead of deriving it from the native payload.
findings.remediation: Emit screenW/screenH (native pixels), densityDpi (e.g. scale*160 or points-per-inch table, documented) and orientation from the extension (it knows the buffer geometry) via result.json, and fill them in ProovraBroadcastResult.toJsMap. Add a golden fixture of the Swift result map shared by a mobile unit test (buildContinuousManifest → validateScreenContinuousManifest) and the API integration test.
findings.requiredTests: Mobile: buildContinuousManifest(fixture-from-Swift-map) passes validateScreenContinuousManifest(expectedPlatform:'ios'). API: uc5 integration test must load the same fixture rather than an inline device literal.
findings.runtimeProbe: In services/api integration harness: open a DIRECT_SCREEN_CAPTURE_IOS session, upload 2 segments + a manifest whose device = {platform:'ios',osVersion:'18.0',model:'iPhone',appVersion:'1.0.0'}, POST /continuous-complete → expect 4xx CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID.

findings.title: The app cannot stop the iOS broadcast: in-app Stop and every controlled stop post a Darwin note the extension never observes, then return a fabricated INTERRUPTED summary while recording continues
findings.userImpact: Tapping 'Stop & Review' (or hitting the byte ceiling / upload backpressure) does not stop recording: the status-bar indicator stays on and the extension keeps writing up to 600 segments into the container. The review shows 'Interrupted' for a session the user ended cleanly; everything recorded after the tap is never emitted or uploaded and is wiped at the next start.
findings.legalImpact: The sealed manifest (if it could seal) would state INTERRUPTED_SESSION/terminationReason INTERRUPTED with captureStartedAtUtc equal to the stop instant and totalDurationMs 0 — false provenance for a clean stop. The client byte/backpressure bounds (SESSION_BOUNDS_REACHED, SEGMENT_UPLOAD_BACKPRESSURE) are unenforceable on iOS.
findings.securityImpact: Recording of the screen continues after the user asked PROOVRA to stop (OS indicator remains visible; user can still stop from Control Center).
findings.reproduction: stopContinuousCapture (Swift :97-105) posts com.proovra.screencapture.ios.finished (:100). SampleHandler registers no Darwin observer at all (whole file; it only POSTS at :136 and :152), so the broadcast keeps running. The app's own observer for that same name (:119-123) fires, emitting onScreenContinuousStopped with readResult(); readResult finds no result.json (the extension only writes it in broadcastFinished/stopBroadcast, SampleHandler.swift:75,86) and returns the fallback (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:136-143): startedAtUtc=endedAtUtc=now, totalDurationMs 0, INTERRUPTED. stopObserving (:103) then removes the handlers, so later segments are never emitted. requestControlledStop (continuous-capture.tsx:105-113) uses the same call.
findings.expected: An app→extension stop channel: the extension observes a stop Darwin note (or polls a stop flag in state.json on each buffer) and calls finishBroadcastWithError / finalizes and writes result.json with USER_STOPPED; the app waits (bounded) for result.json before resolving.
findings.rootCause: The extension side of the stop handshake was never implemented; the app-side comment (:98-99) assumes it exists.
findings.remediation: In SampleHandler.broadcastStarted register a Darwin observer for a dedicated stop name (not the 'finished' name the app itself listens to) that sets a flag; on the next buffer finalize the segment, write result.json (USER_STOPPED/COMPLETE or the client limitation), and finishBroadcastWithError with a user-facing 'stopped from PROOVRA' message. In the module, wait up to N seconds for result.json before reading, and never synthesize startedAtUtc=now.
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance: start broadcast, stop in-app → indicator disappears, result terminationReason USER_STOPPED, last segment emitted. Unit: a Swift-free JS test that the stop path waits for a result instead of accepting the fallback.

findings.title: iOS 'stream while recording' cannot happen: the host app is suspended while the user is in other apps, so segments pile up and the backlog trips the 8-segment backpressure stop on return
findings.userImpact: The screen copy says 'Segments upload in the background' (continuous-capture.tsx:442). On iOS nothing uploads while PROOVRA is backgrounded; on return, the drain emits every accumulated segment at once, captured−uploaded ≥ 8 fires requestControlledStop with 'Uploads fell behind, so recording stopped' — for any recording longer than ~48 s spent outside PROOVRA. Because of UC-IOS-002 the broadcast actually continues, but observing stops, so the rest is lost.
findings.legalImpact: Sessions are labelled with SEGMENT_UPLOAD_BACKPRESSURE and end at the moment the user came back, not when they stopped.
findings.reproduction: app.json ios.infoPlist (:51-69) declares no UIBackgroundModes; ReplayKit runs the extension in its own process while the host app is suspended within seconds of leaving foreground. Darwin posts from the extension are not processed by a suspended app. On resume, the next segmentReady note triggers drainSegments (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.swift:133-139) which emits all pending segments; onSegment (continuous-capture.tsx:153-176) evaluates shouldStopForBackpressure(captured, uploaded, maxPendingSegments=8).
findings.observed: Android-shaped streaming/backpressure policy applied unchanged to iOS.
findings.expected: iOS policy that treats the App Group container as the durable spool: no backpressure stop for a backlog that exists only because the app was suspended; upload on return / on stop; honest copy ('uploads when you return to PROOVRA').
findings.rootCause: Shared UC-3 client flow assumes the host process runs during capture, which is false on iOS.
findings.remediation: Branch the backpressure rule on Platform.OS (container-spooled on iOS, bounded by disk, not by pending count), drain on AppState 'active', and fix the copy. Optionally use a background URLSession from the extension — but the extension's 50 MB ceiling argues for app-side upload.
findings.requiredTests: Unit test of the flow reducer with an iOS burst of 20 segments arriving at once → no controlled stop. Device acceptance: 3-minute broadcast in another app, return, stop → all segments uploaded.

findings.title: Extension segment timing is wrong: the final segment is recorded with durationMs 0 and a start offset equal to the session end, so COMPLETE iOS sessions are refused as having an undeclared gap
findings.userImpact: Even with UC-IOS-001 fixed, a cleanly stopped session whose last segment is longer than 3 s (roughly half of all sessions at 6 s segments) fails Finish & Sign with CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID. Static screens (ReplayKit delivers no new frames when nothing changes) also create >3 s wall-clock gaps between segments.
findings.legalImpact: The last segment's declared duration (0) is false provenance in the manifest.
findings.reproduction: broadcastFinished calls finalizeSegment(durationMs: 0, force: true) (SampleHandler.swift:74). finalizeSegment computes offsetMs = wallElapsed − durationMs (:121) = wallElapsed, and writes durationMs 0 (:126). With result COMPLETE_SESSION/USER_STOPPED (:75), the validator computes between = last.startedAtOffsetMs − (prev.startedAtOffsetMs + prev.durationMs) ≈ the true length of the last segment (:391); > maxGapMs 3000 (:73 of bounds) sets gapFound, and a COMPLETE session with a gap is refused (:402).
findings.observed: Final segment duration hard-coded to 0; offsets mix wall clock and PTS.
findings.expected: Final segment duration = last appended PTS − segmentStartPts; offsets derived from one clock (PTS relative to the first frame of the session).
findings.rootCause: finalizeSegment's force path passes a literal 0 instead of measuring the segment.
findings.remediation: Track lastPts; on force-finalize use lastPts − segmentStartPts; compute startedAtOffsetMs from segmentStartPts − sessionFirstPts. Record a limitation when a segment spans a long no-frame interval rather than letting it read as a gap.
findings.requiredTests: Pure timing function extracted from SampleHandler (or mirrored in TS) with a test: 6 s segments + 4 s final → contiguous offsets, validator accepts COMPLETE.

findings.title: iOS start resolves when the picker is presented, not when the broadcast starts: cancel is undetectable and the UI shows 'Continuous capture active' with nothing recording
findings.userImpact: If the user dismisses Apple's picker (or the undocumented sendActions trigger shows nothing), PROOVRA still shows the active state with a server session and reserved record open; Stop then yields 'No screen segments were captured'.
findings.legalImpact: startContinuousCapture reports osConsentGranted:true and captureStartedAtUtc = picker time before any consent (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.swift:88-90).
findings.reproduction: startContinuousCapture resolves inside DispatchQueue.main.async right after ProovraBroadcastPicker.present (:86-94); present() creates an RPSystemBroadcastPickerView that is never added to a window and fires its button (:170-179). continuous-capture.tsx:237 awaits it and dispatches STARTED (:256). Nothing reads state.json.active or waits for a first segment.
findings.expected: Enter a 'waiting for Start Broadcast' state; transition to active on the extension's first state write / Darwin 'started' note; time out back to intro if none arrives.
findings.rootCause: No 'broadcast started' signal from extension to app (broadcastStarted writes nothing and posts nothing, SampleHandler.swift:35-45).
findings.remediation: Have broadcastStarted write state.json {active:true, startedAtUtc} and post a 'started' Darwin note; the module resolves (or emits an event) on that note; the UI shows a pending state until then. Place the picker in the key window's view hierarchy (hidden) before triggering.
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance: open picker, cancel → UI returns to intro, session discarded.

findings.title: Missing result.json (extension crash / jetsam / not yet finished) is replaced by a fabricated summary: start time = now, duration 0, consent true
findings.userImpact: After an extension kill the review shows an interrupted session of zero duration; the true start time is lost even though the extension wrote it to state.json.
findings.legalImpact: captureStartedAtUtc in the manifest equals captureEndedAtUtc (the stop instant) — a false capture window recorded on an INTERRUPTED seal (the validator skips window checks for INTERRUPTED, screen-continuous-manifest.ts:395-412).
findings.reproduction: readResult (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:133-144): when result.json is absent it returns startedAtUtc: now, endedAtUtc: now, totalDurationMs 0, osConsentGranted true. SampleHandler writes startedAtUtc into state.json on every finalize (:131-133), which readState ignores (:97-106). Also state.json keeps active:true forever after a kill, so getContinuousState reports an active session that does not exist.
findings.observed: Fallback synthesizes values instead of reading recorded ones or leaving them unknown.
findings.expected: Fallback reads startedAtUtc and segmentCount from state.json, derives duration from the last sidecar, records CAPTURE_INTERRUPTED, and clears/ages the active flag.
findings.remediation: Use state.json startedAtUtc + last sidecar offset/duration; add 'CAPTURE_INTERRUPTED' to limitations; treat an active flag older than N segment intervals as stale.
findings.requiredTests: Pure mapping test of the fallback (port to TS or Swift unit test on macOS CI).

findings.title: The extension never inspects AVAssetWriter outcomes: a failed writer (e.g. disk full) stalls capture silently, and a failed/timed-out finish still publishes the segment
findings.userImpact: On low storage the broadcast keeps running with the indicator on while nothing more is recorded and no error is shown. A segment whose finishWriting timed out or failed is still emitted and uploaded as an unplayable ORIGINAL.
findings.legalImpact: A truncated/corrupt mp4 is sealed as a segment of a 'complete' session (its digest is honest, its content is not usable).
findings.reproduction: startWriting() result is ignored (:110). input.append's Bool is ignored (:58). When writer.status becomes .failed, finalizeSegment returns early on every rotation (:118) and writer is never reset, so each subsequent frame is dropped forever. finishWriting is awaited with a 5 s timeout whose result is discarded (:122-124) and writer.status/error is never checked before writing the sidecar (:130) and posting segmentReady (:136). No free-space check anywhere.
findings.expected: On writer failure: write result.json with terminationReason ERROR + limitation, finishBroadcastWithError with a storage message. Only publish a sidecar when status == .completed.
findings.rootCause: Error paths of AVAssetWriter not handled.
findings.remediation: Check startWriting()/append()/status/error; on failure stop the broadcast with an explicit reason; pre-check volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage against maxSegments × expected segment size.
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance with a nearly full device.

findings.title: Orientation is inferred from buffer dimensions and the ReplayKit orientation attachment is ignored: landscape content is recorded sideways and labelled portrait; the extension never reports any limitation
findings.userImpact: Recordings made in landscape play back rotated 90°; no ORIENTATION_CHANGED_DURING_CAPTURE is ever recorded.
findings.legalImpact: Segment orientation metadata in the sealed manifest can be false; limitations are always [] (SampleHandler.swift:149).
findings.reproduction: width/height are taken once from the first buffer (:51) and orientation = width >= height (:128). ReplayKit delivers the device's native buffer geometry and reports rotation via the RPVideoSampleOrientationKey attachment, which is never read (no CMGetAttachment call in the file); no AVAssetWriterInput.transform is set.
findings.observed: Geometry-only orientation, fixed at first frame.
findings.expected: Read RPVideoSampleOrientationKey per buffer, set the writer input transform per segment, rotate segments on orientation change, and add ORIENTATION_CHANGED_DURING_CAPTURE when it changes.
findings.rootCause: Android MediaProjection assumption (buffer geometry follows display rotation) carried to ReplayKit.
findings.proof: source-proven (device behaviour of the attachment per Apple ReplayKit documentation; device confirmation BLOCKED)
findings.remediation: As expected; keep the validator's orientation↔dimension rule satisfied by reporting post-transform dimensions.

findings.title: Broadcast pauses (broadcastPaused/broadcastResumed) are not handled: a paused interval is silently absorbed into a segment and the session is still claimed COMPLETE
findings.userImpact: A pause (system interruption) appears as a frozen stretch inside a segment with no notice.
findings.legalImpact: COMPLETE_SESSION / 'no known interruption' (continuous-capture.tsx:453) is asserted across an interruption the OS reported to the extension.
findings.reproduction: SampleHandler overrides only broadcastStarted, processSampleBuffer and broadcastFinished (:35,:47,:71). A pause yields no frames; the next frame's PTS jump is counted into the current segment's elapsedMs (:62), so the gap never reaches the validator's inter-segment check.
findings.expected: Override broadcastPaused/broadcastResumed; finalize the segment on pause; on finish mark INTERRUPTED_SESSION with CAPTURE_INTERRUPTED (or a new PAUSED limitation).
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance: incoming call / pause during broadcast.

findings.title: No iOS crash/relaunch recovery: the next start wipes the App Group spool, destroying un-uploaded segments of a killed session; broadcasts started from Control Center are silently discarded
findings.userImpact: If PROOVRA is killed during a broadcast (common while the user is in other apps), relaunch shows no session to resume; the recorded segments remain on disk until the next 'Start', which deletes them. The 'PROOVRA Screen Broadcast' entry in Control Center records segments no one ever consumes.
findings.legalImpact: Recorded-but-unsealed capture material is destroyed without the user being told.
findings.securityImpact: Orphaned screen recordings of arbitrary content persist in the App Group container until the next start.
findings.reproduction: sessionRef/declaredRef are in-memory refs (continuous-capture.tsx:88-90); reconnect requires sessionRef.current (:194), which is null after relaunch. startContinuousCapture → beginSession → FileManager.removeItem(uc5-broadcast dir) (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:85). Nothing persists the server captureSessionId/evidenceId for a live iOS recording, and nothing inspects the container at launch.
findings.observed: Recovery exists only while the JS process survives.
findings.expected: Persist {captureSessionId, evidenceId, declared parts} at start; at launch, if the container holds segments or state.active, offer resume/upload or explicit discard; never delete un-uploaded segments without confirmation.
findings.rootCause: The shared continuous screen was designed around a foreground-service Android process that survives app switches.
findings.remediation: As expected; use saveCaptureSession-style durable record at start (it currently runs only at finalize, continuous-capture.tsx:345).
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance: kill app mid-broadcast, relaunch, recover.

findings.title: iOS continuous-capture copy describes Android: 'Android restrictions' and 'stop … from the capture notification' (iOS has no such notification)
findings.userImpact: Wrong instructions at the permission-education moment.
findings.legalImpact: Consent disclosure is inaccurate for iOS users.
findings.reproduction: Only the first bullet branches on isIOS (:422-424); :427, :428 and :442 render unconditionally.
findings.expected: iOS copy: protected (DRM) content appears black per Apple; stop from the red status indicator / Control Center or in PROOVRA.
findings.remediation: Branch the remaining strings on isIOS.
findings.requiredTests: Render test of the intro on Platform.OS='ios'.

findings.title: Darwin observer lifecycle is broken: each registration uses a throw-away NSObject pointer, removeAll never removes them, and drainSegments runs on two threads
findings.userImpact: Repeated sessions accumulate CF observers so each note triggers N drains/N stop events; a race between the Expo queue (stop) and main thread (Darwin callback) on lastEmittedSequence can emit a segment twice, leading to a failed duplicate upload toast or a duplicate partIndex that the validator refuses.
findings.reproduction: observe() passes Unmanaged.passUnretained(NSObject()).toOpaque() (:202) — a new, immediately released object each call; removeAll() passes yet another new pointer (:211), which matches no registered observer. drainSegments (Module :133-139) is called from the AsyncFunction (:101) and from the Darwin callback on main (:117,:121) without synchronization.
findings.expected: One stable observer token (e.g. the module instance), removed with the same token; drain serialized on one queue.
findings.remediation: Use Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) of a long-lived object and serialize drainSegments on a DispatchQueue.

findings.title: No legal/privacy disclosure covers mobile screen recording (UC-2/UC-3/UC-5); only Direct Web Capture has a legal page
findings.userImpact: Users are not told in the privacy notice what a screen recording collects (third-party content, other apps, notifications on screen), where it is stored, or how long.
findings.legalImpact: Screen recordings capture third-party personal data; privacy.md, data-retention.md and evidence-handling.md never mention screen capture/recording, while a dedicated direct-web-capture.md exists. App Store / Play data-safety declarations have no repository source to derive from.
findings.reproduction: grep -niE 'screen (capture|record|broadcast)|replaykit|mediaprojection' apps/web/content/legal/en/*.md → no matches. The only disclosure is in-app intro copy (continuous-capture.tsx:420-430).
findings.observed: No canonical legal text for UC-2/3/5.
findings.expected: A legal page (like direct-web-capture.md) for mobile screen capture, linked from the capture intro, plus privacy-notice and retention entries. [Counsel review required]
findings.rootCause: Legal corpus not extended when UC-2/3/5 shipped.

findings.title: Capture has no monitoring: 0 of 32 alert rules cover direct/screen capture, no capture runbook exists, and alert delivery is not wired in production
findings.userImpact: A 100% failure of iOS seals (UC-IOS-001) or of extension OAuth would raise no alert.
findings.securityImpact: Abuse of capture routes (only session-open is rate-limited) is unobserved.
findings.reproduction: grep -ciE 'capture|direct' infra/grafana/alerts/proovra-operations-alerts.yaml → 0. Contact point url is ${PROOVRA_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL} (no default, by design). docs/uc6-release-acceptance.md:82 records Monitoring FAIL (no evaluator in docker-compose.prod.yml); infra/docker/docker-compose.monitoring.yml exists but deployment is not evidenced.
findings.expected: Metrics + alerts for direct-session open/complete failure rate by acquisitionMode and denial code (CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID, SCREEN_MANIFEST_INVALID, extension OAuth failures), and a capture runbook.
findings.rootCause: Capture features shipped without observability requirements.
findings.requiredTests: Alert-rule lint that every acquisitionMode has a failure-rate rule.

findings.title: Native capture code is never compiled or executed in CI and the extension Playwright e2e runs in no workflow, so the UC-5 'Code PASS' rests on text-level checks and a fabricated server fixture
findings.reproduction: All workflows run on ubuntu-latest; no macOS runner, no xcodebuild, no EAS build step. 'Test — mobile' (ci.yml:260-302) runs node --test (text/offline checks incl. pbxproj-integrity and native-module-contract). playwright-e2e.yml:315 runs root playwright.config.ts --project=chromium (testDir ./e2e); apps/extension/e2e/ has its own config referenced by no workflow (grep 'extension/e2e' .github/workflows → none). ci.yml extension-package job (:908-976) runs extension unit tests + release zip only.
findings.observed: No CI signal for Swift/Kotlin compile or extension e2e.
findings.expected: At minimum a macOS job that runs expo prebuild -p ios + xcodebuild for the app and the ProovraBroadcast target, and a workflow step for apps/extension/e2e.
findings.remediation: Add macos-latest job (prebuild + xcodebuild -sdk iphonesimulator); add the extension e2e project to playwright-e2e.yml.

findings.title: PWA is not installable by Chrome criteria and has no service worker: the manifest has one PNG icon with sizes 'any'
findings.userImpact: No install prompt on Android Chrome; no offline shell; web capture has no offline spool.
findings.reproduction: manifest icons = [{src:'/assets/branding/proovra-mark.png', sizes:'any', type:'image/png'}] (:9-11); 'any' is only meaningful for SVG, and Chrome requires 192px and 512px icons. grep navigator.serviceWorker / serviceWorker.register in apps/web/app,components,lib → none.
findings.expected: 192/512 PNG (+ maskable) icons; a service worker if PWA install is a launch channel — or drop 'PWA' from launch claims.

findings.title: Capture-gating env vars are undocumented: EXTENSION_OAUTH_REDIRECT_ALLOW and NEXT_PUBLIC_EXTENSION_INSTALL_URL appear in no .env.example
findings.userImpact: An operator deploying the extension cannot discover that sign-in fails closed until EXTENSION_OAUTH_REDIRECT_ALLOW is set, or that the install CTA stays 'coming soon' until NEXT_PUBLIC_EXTENSION_INSTALL_URL is inlined at web build time.
findings.reproduction: grep of apps/web/.env.example and services/api/.env.example for both names → none (WORKFLOW_INTAKE_LINKS_ENABLED is documented at services/api/.env.example:303).
findings.observed: Flags live only in code and docs/admin/EXTENSION_RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md prose.
findings.expected: Both documented with defaults in the relevant .env.example.
findings.requiredTests: An env-example parity test over process.env reads in capture code.

findings.title: Release acceptance docs are stale against the tree (AASA placeholder claimed still present; UC-5 device risk named as crypto.subtle)
findings.userImpact: Operators follow a blocker list that no longer matches reality (and misses the real UC-5 blockers above).
findings.reproduction: docs/uc6-release-acceptance.md:272 and :297 say the AASA 'still carries <APPLE_TEAM_ID>'; apps/web/public/.well-known/apple-app-site-association:6 carries 4LCZK75N86 since 92669167 (2026-09-25). uc-disposition.md:88 names crypto.subtle as the device-only hashing risk; apps/mobile/src/upload-utils.ts:11-15,193 uses expo-crypto (Crypto.digest), not crypto.subtle.
findings.expected: Docs updated; the Associated Domains capability (the actual iOS build blocker, :75) stays listed.

appleRestrictions.rule: Broadcast Upload Extension runs in its own process with a ~50 MB memory ceiling (jetsam).
appleRestrictions.respected: partially — streams to disk via AVAssetWriter (no RAM accumulation); full-resolution H.264 with no bitrate cap and a 5 s blocking wait in the sample callback are unmeasured; kill path falls to a fabricated fallback (UC-IOS-006).

appleRestrictions.rule: The host app is suspended in background; no UIBackgroundModes for this use.
appleRestrictions.respected: no — client assumes streaming uploads while recording (UC-IOS-003).

appleRestrictions.rule: Extension cannot be stopped by the host except through its own IPC (the extension calls finishBroadcastWithError).
System shows a recording indicator; DRM/protected content appears black.
appleRestrictions.respected: yes — not suppressed; copy wrongly attributes limits to Android (UC-IOS-011).

appleRestrictions.rule: ReplayKit delivers native-geometry buffers with orientation in RPVideoSampleOrientationKey; frames only when content changes.
Extension and app share data only via App Group container / Darwin notifications.
